cues.en: All right.
In this section we are going to learn about minimum spanning tree.
Now minimum spanning tree is a concept in graph theory that applies to weighted undirected graph.
It is a subgraph that contains all vertices in the graph without forming any cycle, and with the minimum
possible total edge weight.
Now there are key characteristics of minimum spanning tree, so the first one is spanning, which means
that it must include all vertices of the original graph and the second one is three.
So it must be acyclic graph, which means that it's going to be the tree.
And the third one is the minimum, which means that the sum of the weights of the edges in minimum spanning
tree must be the smallest possible among all spanning trees of the graph.
Now, it might be difficult to understand it from this definition.
So that's why, as always, I'm going to provide the real life example.
So let's say we are looking at a problem where we have five island and we need to build the bridge between
them.
But in this case, we need to build the bridge, which is going to cost as low as possible.
So here the question is which bridge should we construct to ensure that all islands are accessible while
minimizing the total cost?
Given that the cost of the bridge between island varies based on the different factors.
So in this picture you can easily see that the cost from this island to this island is 35.
But from this island to this island is five.
And we have old bridge over here.
Now by using minimum spanning tree, we are going to find out the cost effective solution which is going
to be the minimum cost.
Now if we solve this problem using the minimum spanning tree, it's going to be something like this.
So as you can see if we sum up the cost over here it's going to be 40.
So this means that this is the minimum possible option that we can get to build the bridge between these
islands.
Now you might be interested how we got this solution.
So I'm going to explain it in our upcoming lectures here.
You just need to know that this is the solution that we are going to get if we solve it by using minimum
spanning tree.
Now when many people face this problem, they mix this solution with a single source shortest path.
So many people get confused about these two problems.
Now you need to take into account that these solutions of these problems are different.
So if you solve the same problem by using the single source shortest path, the solution is in this
case is going to be like this.
And if you sum up the cost over here, you can easily see that the cost in this case is 50, which is
more than 40.
But in case of minimum spanning tree, we are looking for the solution where the cost is minimum.
So we are not looking for the shortest path.
We are looking at the minimum cost solution, which is in this case this one.
So you need to be very careful not to mix this solution.
So with this example, hopefully you have understood why we need minimum spanning tree in graphs.
